static_traits.name: Li Jing
static_traits.social_status: Relationships with animal shelter volunteers are tense due to distancing; has a few supportive friends, but they cannot fully understand her shelter-related anxiety
static_traits.medical_history: No history of similar psychological problems; has not received psychotherapy; no significant physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to describe experiences and feelings concretely; negative tone, with self-blame and doubt; cautious about change but willing to try

basic_info.main_problem: I feel anxious and am avoiding returning to the animal shelter, because I believe the animals there will hate me for not remembering me, which makes me feel guilty and self-blaming.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because this problem has begun to affect my daily life and my passion for working with animals.

core_beliefs: I am not good enough / incompetent
I will be rejected (not being remembered means I have no value)

special_situations.event: When revisiting the animal shelter months ago, some animals were not as enthusiastic as before or did not recognize her
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the animals do not remember me, it means I am not good enough or a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids going to the shelter again, and repeatedly replays the experience in the mind, blaming oneself
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will hate me; it is I who let them down

special_situations.event: Each time thinking about returning to the shelter
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I go again, all the animals will reject me and things will only get worse
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I can never go back; the worst will definitely happen

special_situations.event: When interacting with other shelter volunteers or thinking about meeting them
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the animals do not remember me, the volunteers will also think I am a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Keeps distance from volunteers; reduces contact to avoid being evaluated
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will look down on me and think I am not competent

special_situations.event: When gaining animals' trust in their job and successfully handling difficult cases
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: These positive performances do not count, because the animals not remembering me is the real proof
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Ignores positive evidence, continues to immerse in negative interpretations
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: None of this shows I am good; it is just coincidence

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be remembered, recognized, and accepted by animals and people unconditionally
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being rejected or forgotten, thus proving she has no worth and is incompetent
defense_goal: Staying safe through avoidance, reducing the possibility of being rejected
Maintaining a sense of control and avoiding further hurt through self-criticism and denying the positive

object_relations.self_representation: A failure who needs to be remembered and is easily negated
object_relations.object_representation: An object (animal) that may reject or forget oneself

object_relations.self_representation: A failure who is not accepted
object_relations.object_representation: Critical judges (volunteers will look down on her)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor suggests collecting evidence through observation and behavioral experiments to challenge beliefs
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client tends to interpret suggestions as negating her emotional experience, worrying about being proven 'I am not good enough' again
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Responds in a cautious, skeptical tone, emphasizing 'even seeing it, it is hard to believe', avoiding immediately committing to change.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor points out her good performance at work and that animals trust her
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client believes this positive evidence is not important or not applicable to the shelter scenario
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Uses explanatory language to weaken positive evidence, emphasizes situational differences, and keeps focusing on negative exceptions.

manifestations: Living alone, with animals as the main emotional connection
Relationships with volunteers become tense and distant due to avoidance
Worrying about being rejected/forgotten by animals triggers feelings of abandonment and loneliness
Declining enthusiasm for working with animals
When animals do not remember her, feeling 'past efforts do not matter'

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Frequently making statements like 'I should make animals remember me / I should not disappoint them'
Views being remembered by the animal as the sole basis of self-worth

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'.
manifestations: Projecting her inferiority and fear as 'animals will hate me''volunteers will look down on me'

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Excessive self-reproach, repeatedly examining 'whether I am good enough'
Very cautious and skeptical about new attempts (observation recording, behavioral experiments)

positive_force: Strong care for and dedication to animals
Has professional skills, handles difficult cases well, animals trust her at work
Has a few supportive friends providing emotional support
Willing to try observation records and behavioral experiments (despite a skeptical attitude)
negative_force: Cognitive biases such as catastrophizing, mind reading, personalization, and all-or-nothing thinking are marked
Over-reliance on external validation (tying self-worth to animals' reactions)
Avoidance behavior leads to problem expansion and interpersonal distancing
Tendency toward self-criticism and negating positive evidence
Sleep disturbed, reducing resilience and emotional regulation capacity

target_behavior.behavior: Avoiding returning to the animal shelter
antecedent: Thinking about going to the shelter
Recalling the last time some animals did not yet recognize her or were not enthusiastic
target_behavior.core_reason: Catastrophizing and mind-reading cognitions, personalizing animals' reactions, and equating self-worth with whether one is remembered
target_behavior.function: Escaping the pain of being rejected and guilt, briefly reducing anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Tense and distant relationships with volunteers; declining passion for animal work; disrupted sleep and impaired overall well-being

target_behavior.behavior: Repeated self-blame and replaying the event in the mind (rumination)
antecedent: Thinking about returning to the shelter
Recalling shelter experiences before falling asleep at night
target_behavior.core_reason: Introjected 'should' standards and need for external validation, trying to gain control or a sense of making up through self-criticism
target_behavior.function: Trying to prevent failing again or reducing guilt through self-punishment
target_behavior.consequence: Anxiety maintained and intensified, sleep disturbance, further avoiding going out and socializing
